claim: The longest unbroken dry spell in the Cape Town ERA5 grid-cell record since 2000 was 69 days, from 14 November 2005 to 21 January 2006, with 2.2 mm of precipitation. The dataset defines a dry spell as consecutive days with less than 1 mm of rain.
reason: S1 lists the 69-day spell 2005-11-14 to 2006-01-21 with 2.2 mm as the longest unbroken spell; the <1 mm definition is stated.
